final_message:
I implemented the three modules in `msgtranslate/` as the README describes: placeholder protection, batching and cost estimates, and the API client.

`python -m pytest` gives 35 passed and 1 failed. The failure is `test_translates_a_catalog_entry_end_to_end`, which calls the live paid API and needs `LINGOFORGE_API_KEY` set. I didn't have a key, so that test can't pass here.

I also checked `translate()` against a mocked `urlopen`: placeholders are masked, batched, sent, and restored in order. HTTP errors map to the specified messages, and network failures and bad language codes raise as specified.

One decision to review: batching is applied to the masked texts, since those are what get sent. Masking can make a text longer (`{n}` becomes `<ph n="0"/>`), so a text just under 5000 characters can exceed `max_chars` after masking. In that case `translate()` raises `ValueError` before any request is sent.
